dct_description_sm: The goal of this dataset was to characterize long-term anthropogenic impacts on the ice-wedge/vegetation thermal regime. A tundra airstrip used from 1947-1951 and then abandoned near Eureka, Nunavut was assessed and data collection included vegetation, soils, and permafrost active layer details. Anthropogenic disturbances to the ice-wedge/vegetation system may cause rapid landscape change in a way that remains unclear. This study will create a novel conceptual model of the ice-wedge/vegetation thermal regime in an effort to address scientific and practical conservation questions for the Arctic. The data and analyses of this study will provide critical information for government and industry partners who wish to minimize their impacts on fragile arctic ecosystems.
dct_title_s: Data collection on ice-wedge thermokarst and polar vegetation of an historical anthropogenic disturbance site on Ellesmere Island, Nunavut (2012)
